cells.tense: You are moving from what you actually feel, and the direction holds.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing that matters most and give it the next hour. Let the rest wait.
cells.core:
A pull arrives and it has a direction. You follow it without needing the whole argument first — the sense of what matters comes ahead of the explaining, and the feet keep up. What gets your hours has a reason behind it, and the reason isn't whatever landed on you that morning.
Nothing here needs fixing today. Going well looks like being able to name the one thing getting your time and say why the rest can wait. The cost is that attention rarely gets applause. Nobody hands out credit for the meetings you never took or the openings you let close. Keep spending it anyway, and say out loud what you spent it on.
cells.sheetLine: You feel it, you see what matters, and you move.
cells.verb: channeling what you feel into a direction you keep
cells.place: in the room where attention is being spent

cells.tense: You are already driving past the place you meant to arrive at.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're pushing on right now and don't touch it for a day. Let it sit.
cells.core:
The motion is running ahead of the feeling, and each thing you finish opens a next thing to chase. This one has a shape you're bracing against before it arrives, and the bracing has become its own engine. Speed stops meaning anything when nothing is arriving.
Going well looks like the pull and the pace staying in the same hands — direction from what actually moves you, not from what might need you next. Between those two, something has to be able to go untouched. Choose one thing and leave it a full day; you'll find out whether it was ever yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're driving past the destination and calling it momentum.

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that has already closed behind you.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're finished with, out loud, to one person. Then leave it alone.
cells.core:
Feeling is coming through and stopping at the sill. There's a door in front of you — a move half-begun, a direction kept warm — and you've stood there long enough that hovering has a routine to it. The feeling isn't missing. The forward end of it is.
Going well looks like a pull that arrives, gets noticed, and turns into a next step without a meeting first. What opens that here isn't effort — it's letting one thing be done, because a direction can't take the space another one is squatting in. Pick one ending and say it's finished where it can be heard.
cells.sheetLine: The feeling is there. The forward step isn't.

cells.tense: You are steering without knowing your hand is on the wheel.
cells.ask: Put your name on one direction you've been calling the situation's. Then keep going.
cells.core:
Direction is coming from somewhere and it isn't argued for — the pull shows up, attention lands, the next move follows. The description, though, credits everything else: the workload, the way things are, what needed doing. What's running is yours. What's spoken is borrowed.
Going well looks like a pull recognized, a next thing chosen, and a sentence saying so without ceremony. Nothing needs dismantling tonight. Take one direction you've been calling the situation's and use a word that puts you in the sentence — not a speech, a fact. The moving settles a little once the claim catches up with it.
cells.sheetLine: The wheel is under your hand. The claim isn't.
